headline: A robotics paper shows hidden cross-module error dependence can break downstream uncertainty calibration
summary: A September 20, 2026 arXiv paper analyzes how uncertainty estimates from separately calibrated robotic modules can fail when combined if their errors are correlated. It studies a two-module moving-obstacle example in which position and velocity errors share fixed Gaussian marginals while their correlation varies. The authors report that individual 95% coverage stayed near nominal, but downstream coverage under an independence assumption ranged from 99.98% at correlation -0.9 to 86.46% at +0.9. In a simulated crossing controller, positive dependence increased collisions to 39.7 per 10,000 trials under the independence interface versus 8.7 with oracle joint covariance; joint-covariance estimation restored coverage near 95%, while robust bounds reduced risk at a conservatism cost. This is a controlled simulation result, not evidence of failure rates in physical robots or deployed stacks.
